A release of fixes from a full review of lazybw, plus a few things the guide
promised and lazybw did not do yet. Your configuration keeps working as it
is; the key bindings use the same names as before.

## What's new

- Actions on many items at once no longer freeze lazybw. A few hundred
  marked items used to stop the interface, and past about 800 it hung for
  good with only part of the change sent.
- `q` waits for changes that are still on their way to Bitwarden instead of
  stopping the CLI before they were sent. `:q!` still leaves at once.
- Dialogs act on what they showed. "Delete permanently?" names and counts
  the items it deletes, marks end with the action that used them, and a
  click behind a dialog no longer changes its target.
- The server picked on the login screen is the one lazybw logs in to.
- The automatic lock counts time spent asleep, a lock no longer waits for a
  running health check or export, and locking clears the clipboard only if
  it still holds what lazybw copied.
- Secure notes show their line count in the list, not their first line.
- The editor saves what it shows. Websites, notes from `$EDITOR`, `gE` and
  `Ctrl-s` in the notes editor all had cases where a change did not reach
  the saved item.
- Renaming or deleting a folder changes every folder with that name
  (Bitwarden allows duplicates, and lazybw showed them as one).
- `:gen 32` and `:gen phrase 6` generate and copy, `:sort name!` reverses,
  and the command line keeps its history between sessions.
- `Ctrl-w` and `Ctrl-u` work in every text field, `Ctrl-f` pages down, the
  page motions use the height of the screen, and the mouse wheel scrolls the
  pane under the pointer.
- lazybw writes the log that `lazybw doctor` and the troubleshooting guide
  point to.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SyscallBrain/lazybw/blob/v1.2.0/CHANGELOG.md)
has the full list.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `lazybw-1.2.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any Linux on x86_64 (static binary) |
| `lazybw-1.2.0-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any Linux on ARM64, including Termux on Android |
| `lazybw_1.2.0-1_amd64.deb`, `lazybw_1.2.0-1_arm64.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives |
| `lazybw-1.2.0-1.x86_64.rpm`, `lazybw-1.2.0-1.aarch64.rpm` | Fedora, openSUSE, RHEL and derivatives |
| `lazybw-1.2.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`, `lazybw-1.2.0-1-aarch64.pkg.tar.zst` | Arch Linux, Arch Linux ARM |
| `SHA256SUMS` | checksums of all of the above |

On Arch Linux it is also in the AUR, as `lazybw-bin` (this release's binary)
and `lazybw` (built from source).

The container image with `bw` included is on the GitHub Container Registry:

```sh
docker run -it --rm -v lazybw:/home/lazybw ghcr.io/syscallbrain/lazybw:1.2.0
```

lazybw needs the official Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) 2025.9.0 or newer. The
[user guide](https://syscallbrain.github.io/lazybw/) covers installation and
everything else.
